- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00 or 0.25) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase downward bias or adjust for mean reversion.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak and introduce early mean-reversion decay.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often drifts toward historical mean — apply smoothing or adjust for recent volatility.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is positive — reduce forecast by 2–5% for positive sentiment windows.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a peak, model often fails to anticipate — add lagged correction term or use sentiment as trigger for downward bias.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often overestimates upside — apply sentiment-weighted downward adjustment (e.g., -0.15 to -0.30 per sentiment unit).
